# Policy-KB bijection audit — financing_plan_desk / task 1

Auditor: fresh agent, independent of the renderer and of the policy-side auditor.
Revision 1. Written after `runtime_context/financing_plan_desk/1.md`'s `blind_answer` was
frozen to disk (hash `8cf30eb2ead2c8d103e092695e8bab91f8ad578368b113dc1f91440b787f4c02`).
Audited and recorded separately from task 0; task 0's conclusions do not stand in for this one.

**Entry conditions (Step 0), checked and cited.**
- Policy-side verdict: `financing_plan_desk` passed the source-layer audit at revision 2 —
  task 0 PASS, task 1 PASS on all four relationships (supplied with the brief).
- `check_docs.py` on product `financing` and `check_traceability.py` on this difficulty were
  both green in the coordinator's snapshot; re-run on the final form at close-out (output lines
  at the foot of this file).
- The runtime-visible view and a tool-shaped DB access path were both supplied.
- The gate snapshot with its actual output lines came with the brief.
Nothing is missing; no "incomplete input" is reported.

**Scope of this file.** Task 1's `charter_scope` claims the extended policies
`financing_ext_cycle_statement`, `financing_ext_service_recovery_giveback`,
`financing_ext_schedule_rebuild` and `financing_ext_hardship_schedule`, and the task tools
`issue_cycle_statement_c71da302`, `apply_service_recovery_giveback_b70a9c9e`,
`update_scheduled_payment_2c04479a` and `confirm_hardship_schedule_eb08e7db`. The scan covers
those four policies in their **whole domain**, every base policy governing their subjects
(`financing_evt_statement_cycle`, `financing_courtesy_waiver`, `financing_return_credit`,
`financing_hardship_arrangement`, `financing_evt_late_fee`, `financing_evt_payment_allocation`,
`financing_delinquency_and_charge_off`), the term parameters they read, and the four tool
contracts — including branches this seed never triggers.

## kb_to_source

Sentence-by-sentence over the 28 documents in this task's domain (4 hubs, 4 baselines,
20 factors, and the policy/facet documents above).

- **Every normative claim has a structured source.** A mechanical sweep of every sentence of
  the four extended `rule`s and of all 15 base-policy `rule`s and their `eligibility.condition`s
  against the corpus found **no** sentence in this task's domain without a home; the single
  sentence that failed that sweep across the product belongs to
  `financing_ext_settlement_figure`, which is not in this task's `charter_scope` and is
  recorded in `policy_kb/financing_plan_desk/0.md`. In the reverse direction no prose sentence
  in this domain was found that lacks a source.
- **Added policy: none.** No confirmation step, no review, no notification, no escalation, no
  fallback procedure, no checklist, no numbered workflow. The keyword sweep over all 71
  documents for 26 such patterns returned nothing.
- **Equivalent restatements checked, not assumed.** `hardship_arrangement_enrolment_a1ff956e`'s
  points-of-judgement table restates the source's enrolment standings row by row ("Applied,
  approved, settled, written off or cancelled | Not a state in which an arrangement is
  enrolled") — a permutation of the same clause into a table, admitting exactly the same
  standings, no more and no fewer. `cycle_interest_day_count_convention_30d517df` renders
  "a year of three hundred and sixty days" in words rather than as 360 and then computes with
  it in its table; the boundary is unchanged.
- **Prerequisite-side check 1 — cross-problem operational guidance: none.** No blocked
  problem's document says "if unsatisfied, please call X first", names another problem's tool,
  or names the resolving action or problem beside a state-form sentence. Each of the seven
  task-tool names occurs in exactly one document, its own hub's invocation block
  (machine-checked over all 71). In particular `scheduled_payment_rebuild_6b987eed`, which
  carries **two** prerequisite sentences, names only `update_scheduled_payment_2c04479a` — its
  own tool — and neither `issue_cycle_statement_c71da302` nor
  `apply_service_recovery_giveback_b70a9c9e`.
- **Prerequisite-side check 2 — task world state written in as policy fact: none.** No document
  contains either customer's name, any plan, ledger, work-order, commission, receipt or
  statement reference from either task's world, either frozen date, or a phrase of the form
  "this customer currently…". Every illustration is marked hypothetical and uses figures
  belonging to no seeded record.
- **Aggregation:** no document gathers several problems' prerequisites into a table, checklist
  or route. (Recorded under `dependency_form`.)

## bijection_verdict

**PASS.**

- Every normative atom of the four extended policies in this task's `charter_scope`, and of
  the seven base policies governing their subjects, is borne in the published corpus with
  meaning unchanged and at the same strength — including every untriggered branch: the
  settled-payment and neither-return-nor-settled statement readings; the billing-since and
  two-month statement stretches; the arrangement-in-force presentation share of nothing; the
  monthly-premium coverage rows this coverage does not take; the no-give-back-in-stretch and
  past-due give-back readings; the two-or-more repeated-failure band; the never-been-back
  workshop band; the arrears and term's-own payment factors; the penalty and unreduced rebuild
  rates; the past-due and no-give-back balance-adjustment readings; the 365-day past-due and
  nominal-cycle interest conventions; the past-due catch-up; the below-the-floor and
  no-return arrangement bases; the past-due and mid-term arrangement lengths; the
  repeat-arrangement share and charge; the two-or-more-returns arrangement interest; and the
  design-approval commitment relief. Each is stated in figures in its own factor document, for
  all six promotional terms and not only the one this plan is written on.
- All three `prerequisite` sentences of this task's tree stand verbatim, in their declared
  **state** form, with their ordering connectives and strength intact, each in a document of the
  policy it blocks and in no other policy's; all three hops are resolvable at the source's
  strength from the sentence, the depended-on documents and the records.
- All four baselines are complete and self-sufficient; each of the twenty declared factors'
  whole ladders is carried in its own factor document with every tier exact.
- The retired surface is exact for all four `overwrite` declarations in this domain: each
  superseded clause is quoted verbatim and marked no longer in force in the base policy's own
  bearing document, each such document keeps the rest of its policy as clauses in force, and
  the corpus retires nothing the source did not.
- No claim from outside the source appears in the prose.

**Relation to previous revisions.** None; this is revision 1 for this difficulty.

## dependency_form

Basis: the hop marks frozen in `runtime_context/financing_plan_desk/1.md` (all three hops
**state-derived**, none pre-solved) and a read of the whole 71-document product corpus.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| A state-form prerequisite sentence restated as an action, or naming the performer or the other problem | **None.** All three sentences speak only of what the record must carry or be — "carries in the billing history the statement that cycle presented", "must already stand answered by a give-back in the billing history", "answers the balance the plan owes at the handling date". None is restated anywhere as an act, an actor or a policy. The second sentence names the *ground* on which a charge arose ("that a failure of the chain's own handling brought about"), which is how the source itself identifies the state and is not the naming of an action or a performer |
| A restatement of either form naming a tool, a policy or another document | **None.** Machine-checked over all 71 documents for the seven task-tool names: each occurs in exactly one document, its own hub, under its own "Invoking `<tool>`" heading. No policy id appears in any document; no document quotes another's title |
| A dependency or an order between problems that no prerequisite sentence states, or one of the source's dependencies stated in a second document | **None.** Each of the five `policy_source` strings in the product occurs verbatim in exactly one document, and that document is the blocked policy's hub. `cycle_statement_issue_09393dd2` and `service_recovery_give_back_booking_9c2e12f2` — the depended-on side of this task's two second-level hops — carry only their own rules and disclose nothing about who waits on them |
| A dependency table, checklist, roadmap, complete route, or several problems strung into an ordered step list | **None.** This is the sharpest test in this difficulty, because `scheduled_payment_rebuild_6b987eed` is simultaneously a blocked problem and a depended-on one. It states its two conditions as two sentences under "Conditions on the figure" and stops; it does not mention the arrangement that waits on it, does not order its two conditions against each other, and does not gather the three-level tree anywhere. No document in the product lists more than its own policy's conditions |
| Cross-problem operational guidance ("if unmet, first call X"), another problem's tool named inside a blocked problem's documents, or the resolving action named beside a state-form sentence | **None**, on the same machine check plus a keyword sweep for 26 route and procedure patterns across all 71 documents, which returned nothing |
| A contrast between a wrong and a correct reading, a named mistake, or an example or FAQ walking across problems | **None.** The training-note genre used by several factor documents asks basis questions ("Which reading governs where more than one might?") and answers them inside that document's own ladder; no question walks to another problem, and no example demonstrates the chain |
| A title or opening mirroring a task's situation | **None.** "Taking Up a Replacement Payment Arrangement on a Belrose Promotional Financing Plan", "Closing a Billing Cycle on a Belrose Promotional Financing Plan", "Setting the Payment a Belrose Promotional Financing Plan Bills Each Cycle" and "Putting Right a Failure of the Chain's Own Handling on a Belrose Promotional Financing Plan" name the request type or the event type their policies are defined by — the general subject. None names a customer, a standing, a figure or a circumstance of this seed; every opening begins from the general case ("A customer who cannot meet the ordinary schedule … may take up a replacement payment arrangement") |
| A depended-on document reachable only through phrasing borrowed from the dependent document | **No.** Both second-level hubs are reachable through the words the records use. The runtime `KB_search` on "statement for the cycle amount presented" — built from `financing_statement_issued` and the plan's `statement_day` — returns the statement documents at rank 1; the give-back hub is titled in the same words the sentence and the ledger's `waiver_reason_code service_recovery` use. The first-level hub, `scheduled_payment_rebuild_6b987eed`, is titled "Setting the Payment a Belrose Promotional Financing Plan Bills Each Cycle", which is the plan record's own `scheduled_monthly_payment` in business words |
| A factor document saying which tier a customer, or most customers, fall on; describing the reading a person without the rule would take as the mistake; or writing a task's evidence rows in as fact | **None.** All 20 factor documents in this domain state their ladder as a rule and leave the tier to be derived. Illustrations are explicitly hypothetical and use figures belonging to no seeded record ("A commission in production with 2,400.00 USD still to pay: 15.00 USD").
